title: Backfill: populate missing provenance + compatibility for top 50 catalog models (dry-run + audit summary)
author: Michael Nguyen
commits: migrations: add top50 provenance/compat mapping table + normalizers
backfill: implement dry-run planner + apply path with idempotency
audit: emit summary JSON + per-record diff for review workflow
tests: fixture models + validate required fields before/after backfill
description:
Context
We’re migrating existing catalog entries onto Model Metadata Schema v1. During staging validation we still have missing/partial values in two areas that are required for customer-facing changelogs and enterprise change-management: (1) provenance (provider/source, base model lineage, and weights/license references) and (2) compatibility matrix (hosted/dedicated/private availability and feature compat flags like tool/function calling and structured output).

This PR introduces a one-time backfill tool for the top 50 catalog models (by usage) to populate missing provenance + compatibility fields with Redwood-approved values and consistent formatting. This unblocks schema validation enforcement and reduces "surprise" output changes without an accompanying changelog entry (ref: SUP-18455).

What’s included
- New CLI: cmd/backfill_model_metadata
  - Supports dry-run planning mode (default) and explicit apply mode.
  - Produces an audit summary artifact that can be attached to the review workflow (and later emitted as a signed change-event).
- Backfill logic for top 50 models only (explicit allowlist)
  - Each entry includes:
    - provenance.provider (e.g., "meta", "mistral", "qwen", "open-source")
    - provenance.source (HF repo / vendor page URL when available)
    - provenance.license (SPDX-ish string when known, otherwise "unknown" but flagged)
    - provenance.base_model (normalized base identifier when the served model is a fine-tune/instruct)
    - compatibility.deployment_modes (hosted/dedicated/private)
    - compatibility.features (structured_output, function_calling/tool_calling, json_mode, embeddings, reranking)
    - compatibility.constraints (min_runtime_version, known_incompatibilities)
- Idempotency + safety
  - Only writes fields when currently null/empty (no clobber), unless --overwrite is explicitly passed.
  - Validates post-write record against schema_v1 required fields (fails the run if a write would still leave the record invalid).
  - Rate-limits and retries registry updates to avoid overwhelming control plane.
- Audit outputs
  - summary.json: totals + per-model status (planned/updated/skipped/error) + field-level counts
  - diffs.jsonl: one JSON diff per model (old vs new for only changed fields)

CLI usage
- Dry-run (default; no writes):
  backfill_model_metadata --env=staging --top=50 --out=./artifacts
- Apply (writes):
  backfill_model_metadata --env=staging --top=50 --apply --out=./artifacts
- Apply with overwrite (should not be needed for initial run):
  backfill_model_metadata --env=staging --top=50 --apply --overwrite --out=./artifacts

Example dry-run output
Planned updates: 50
- updated: 0
- skipped (already complete): 12
- planned (missing fields): 38
Missing field counts (planned):
- provenance.provider: 14
- provenance.source: 27
- provenance.license: 31
- compatibility.deployment_modes: 9
- compatibility.features.function_calling: 22

Notes / decisions
- Allowlist is intentionally hardcoded for v1 to avoid accidentally backfilling long-tail models without review.
- Licenses: if license cannot be confidently sourced, we set "unknown" and add a compatibility.constraints.known_incompatibilities note: "license_unverified" (this is internal-only; not exposed to customer changelog). Quentin asked that we keep the public surface clean; the generator will rely on allowlisted customer-safe fields.
- We normalize provider names to a stable set (meta/mistral/qwen/google/open-source) to avoid churn in changelog templates.

Testing
- Unit tests for normalizers and mapping table completeness.
- Fixture-based integration test that runs planner over a snapshot of 50 fixture records and asserts:
  - no writes in dry-run
  - apply path is idempotent
  - post-write validation passes

Rollout plan
1) Run dry-run in staging and attach artifacts to ENG-4924.
2) PM/release-eng review the diffs.jsonl for any customer-visible wording concerns.
3) Run apply in staging.
4) Repeat in prod during a low-traffic window with Connor on point.

Review discussion (highlights)
- Quentin Harris (2026-01-27): "Please ensure provider/source normalization doesn’t bake in internal nicknames; also confirm we don’t overwrite existing provenance."
  - Michael Nguyen: "Ack. Provider list is canonicalized; tool only fills missing fields by default. Added guard + tests; updated README to clarify."
- Connor O'Brien (2026-01-27): "Need a clear artifact for change-management signoff. Can we emit a single summary + per-record diffs with stable ordering?"
  - Michael Nguyen: "Added summary.json + diffs.jsonl with deterministic ordering by model_id; also includes run_id and git sha."
- Jordan Lee (2026-01-28): "Any chance this writes internal-only fields that could leak later?"
  - Michael Nguyen: "Tool only touches provenance + compatibility sections. Internal-only notes are stored in compatibility.constraints with a flag that’s not part of the public allowlist (enforced separately in PR-260)."
- Leila Farouk (2026-01-28): "Can we add a test that proves we never clobber existing non-empty fields unless --overwrite?"
  - Michael Nguyen: "Added TestApply_DoesNotOverwriteNonEmptyFields and a fixture with prefilled provenance.source." 

CI
- build: pass
- unit tests: pass
- lint: pass

Merge
Squash merged on 2026-01-28.

Follow-ups

- After PR-219 (change-event emission) lands, we should have the backfill tool optionally emit a signed change-event per updated model rather than just local artifacts (not in scope here).
